title: A cell cutting off under ~3/10 of its volume uses a curved corner wall, not a plane

fields.label: Label
fields.value: A cell cutting off under ~3/10 of its volume uses a curved corner wall, not a plane

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: When a cubical or rectangular cell divides unequally and the smaller part is less than about three-tenths of the whole, the minimal partition is a quarter-cylinder cutting off one corner rather than a plane wall; below about 0.15 of the volume a spherical octant in a corner is smaller still.

fields.label: Notation
fields.value: unequal division of a cube: quarter-cylinder in a corner minimal for V_{small}/V \lesssim 0.3; spherical octant for V_{small}/V \lesssim 0.15

fields.label: Chapter
fields.value: Ch. VIII: The Forms of Tissues, or Cell-Aggregates (continued)

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: that one portion by anything less than about three-tenths of the whole, or three-sevenths of the other portion, there will be a tendency for the cell to divide, not by means of a plane transverse partition, but by means of a curved, cylindrical wall cutting off one corner of the original cell

fields.label: Agent
fields.value: delphisci On Growth and Form claim extractor

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: D’Arcy Wentworth Thompson, On Growth and Form (1st ed., Cambridge: Cambridge University Press, 1917), Chapter VIII, “The Forms of Tissues, or Cell-Aggregates (continued)”; topic “Unequal division of a cubical cell”. Scope: unequally dividing rectangular plant cells, e.g. hairs in Fucus conceptacles, moss paraphyses, stomatal precursor cells

fields.label: Notation
fields.value: unequal division of a cube: quarter-cylinder in a corner minimal for V_{small}/V \lesssim 0.3; spherical octant for V_{small}/V \lesssim 0.15

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on thompson1917-ch08-03: partially-resolvable, resolvability 0.71

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: The numerical thresholds and wall geometries are highly falsifiable. Public plant imaging can test examples, but adequate sample sizes near both thresholds and across the named tissues are uncertain.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: For rectangular cells with known daughter-volume ratios, classify new walls as planar, quarter-cylindrical, or spherical-octant-like and test transitions near 0.30 and 0.15.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Suitable 3D unequal divisions are a small subset of archived images.

Cell corners and boundary constraints are not ideal cubes.

data existence: 0.58
analysis feasibility: 0.72
discriminating power: 0.9

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: The volume thresholds are numerically explicit, so the pattern would be decisive if cubical cells with known daughter volumes were archived. Public embryo volumes offer some unequal divisions and not the corner-cutting geometry of the named hairs and precursors. The rule can be probed on a proxy tissue and cannot yet be resolved for the cells it was stated about.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: For unequal divisions of roughly cubical cells, plot partition shape against the volume fraction cut off. Curved corner walls below about three-tenths, and spherical octants below about 0.15, with plane walls above the threshold, would support the claim; plane walls remaining common below three-tenths would refute it.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Fucus hairs, moss paraphyses and stomatal precursors, the cases named for this corner geometry, are not in the embryo collection.

Two-dimensional sections underestimate the difference between a quarter-cylinder and a plane.
